newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Spill reported at Nigerian Agip crude oil pipe.
newsitem.headline: Spill reported at Nigerian Agip crude oil pipe.

text.p: An unknown amount of crude oil has spilled from an Agip pipeline in southeastern Nigeria that may have been sabotaged, the national news agency reported on Tuesday.
The News Agency of Nigeria said the spillage happened between Akiri and Ebochco in the southeastern Rivers state.
A local chief, Eze Uzor, was quoted as saying the oil had polluted a large area of farmland and was spreading into surrounding creeks. Uzor blamed pipe corrosion for the spillage.
But Agip spokesman Akin Aruwajoye put the spill down to sabotage.
"It couldn't have been pipe decay as they are barely 15 years old and are well protected," Aruwajoye said.
Oil companies working onshore in Nigeria have accused local people of sabotaging pipelines in the search for compensation money paid by oil companies for damaged land.
Acts of sabotage by Ken Saro-Wiwa's Movement for the Survival of Ogoni People (MOSOP) forced Shell to quit Ogoniland, in the same Rivers state in 1993.
Shell have been under fire from campaigners since November when Saro-Wiwa and eight other minority rights activists were hanged for murder in spite of international appeals for clemency.
